explanation:
The central tree retains the seed's seven conceptual branches while shrinking from 103 to 71 lines (31.1%) and from 6,793 to 4,708 characters (30.7%). Six peripherals expand ownership, gesture calls, selection, rendering dependencies, routing, and persistence. Modular boundaries follow responsibilities and exposed interfaces rather than source-file containment. Edges attach to the concepts being expanded; positions leave measured gaps between all diagram bounds.

Source-grounded qualifications: selectionState.ts:75-81 supports rectangle-based membership for legacy regions without explicit IDs. shapeProjection.ts:26-43 excludes non-conversation viewport panes and code-panel/source-code projection panes from native floating-shape projection, qualifying the seed's broad visibility claim. canvasSession.ts:69-84 publishes changed controller slices synchronously but invokes commit listeners only when canvasRevisionId changes. MappingPage.tsx:283-458 shows explicit flush barriers in particular handlers; generic apply and copy-document return without their own explicit flush, so acknowledgement is not presented as a universal durability guarantee.

Details added beyond the seed include copyDocument resetting selection, controls and pending conversation requests (canvasWorkspace.ts:42-58); clone-batch rejection and collapsed conversation anchors (MappingEditorRuntime.ts:144-188); expansion and measurement rules (displayModel.ts:114-146); shape exclusions, bubble dimensions and connection-focus invalidation (shapeProjection.ts and CanvasRuntimeContext.tsx); and worker failure invalidation (NativeRoutingStore.ts:86-115).

Only context.json and seed.json supplied evidence. Calls describe paths visible in source, not observed runtime traces. Controller, persistence adapter, receiver and worker implementations are not pinned; their internal behavior is not inferred beyond the supplied call sites.
